subject: research/ambient-fullinfo
professional: a machine-learning researcher in off-policy / counterfactual learning (contextual bandits, inverse-propensity and doubly robust estimators, covariate shift); first checks: does the fitting routine actually reach the estimator it claims to compute, is the selection mechanism ignorable given the features (in which case a correctly specified unweighted MLE is already consistent), is there a label-matched control, and is the result positioned against Shimodaira 2000, Strehl et al. 2010, Swaminathan and Joachims 2015 and Dudik et al. 2011

evidence.correctness: The arithmetic pipeline reproduces (rerun of experiments/run.py in a scratch copy: results.txt identical, 5 min 07 s), and the oracle reference is right: a closed-form Bayes posterior from the World parameters (/tmp/claude-0/round94-ambient/chk/analytic.py) gives true weights [2.0, 2.242, 0, -5.991] against the code's 2000 h fit [1.998, 2.263, -0.019, -6.002], and expected utility 12.52/h against the held-out 12.71 +- 0.13 (SE over 20 streams). But the estimator is not what the README says it is. fit_map (core.py:44-58) takes 40 undamped Newton steps with no line search and no convergence check. An independent damped-Newton MAP solver with Armijo backtracking on the exact (unclipped) objective (/tmp/claude-0/round94-ambient/chk/mapcheck.py) on 12 hour-100 fits: for every uninformed biased fit and 4 of 6 IPS fits checked, the code's weights have MAP objective 450x to 360,000x the true minimum (e.g. 47,679 vs 105.0; 456,879,705 vs 1,285.8), gradient norm 490 to 32,000, and distance from the prior mean 163 to 29,972 against the bound sqrt(2 J(w0)) = 33 to 117 that any true MAP must satisfy. The true MAPs lie 1.2 to 10 from the oracle. Rerunning the whole experiment with the converged solver (/tmp/claude-0/round94-ambient/fixed, 4 min 21 s): hour-100 uninformed biased 10.63/10.85/11.44 (README: 1.59/-0.15/-13.08), uninformed IPS 9.61/11.15/12.36 (README: -23.80/-32.73/-45.55), all weight distances < 3 (README: 179-658 and thousands); informed rows nearly unchanged except the eps=0.002 IPS distance (1501 -> 2.83). Half the result table, and the headline 'fails entirely with the uninformed prior', is an optimizer artifact.
evidence.completeness: Everything listed runs: 4 tests pass (0.98 s), run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte, the README table matches results.txt in all 18 cells (script check, 0 mismatches), experiments/figure.py and utility.svg exist. The stated limitations and next steps (label-matched control, clipped/self-normalised/DR weights) are listed as not done, not claimed. Completeness is of what it says it did; what it did is wrong in half the rows (scored under correctness and claims).
evidence.verification: `cd research/ambient-fullinfo && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q tests`: 4 passed in 0.98 s. Five mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 survived (IPS weights prop instead of 1/prop; full fit on labelled windows only, i.e. full == biased; decision rule ignoring the others-present cost; prior gradient centred on 0 instead of w0) and 1 caught (snapshot hour off by one). No test checks that fit_map converges or that its output is stationary for the objective, which is the defect that broke the results. Scores are before the fix: this round added 3 tests (decision threshold, fit_map stationarity with a non-zero prior mean, full fit on every window) that kill the decide, prior-gradient and full-fit mutants; 7 tests pass. The IPS-weight mutant still survives. The eps=1 test exercises the one regime where biased, IPS and full coincide, so it cannot tell them apart.
evidence.craft: Read src/ambient_fullinfo/core.py (162 lines), tests/test_fullinfo.py, experiments/run.py. Small and readable, but: fit_map is a copied engine (same undamped Newton in research/ambient-ips/src/ambient_ips/ips.py:46 and research/ambient-bandit/src/ambient_bandit/bandit.py:46) that silently returns non-converged weights (no line search, no step cap, no flag); sigmoid clipping at +-30 (core.py:39) zeroes the Hessian contribution of saturated points, which makes the undamped steps worse; run_online is dead code here (not used by run.py or tests); run.py is a top-level script with no testable function; results.txt prints the 'labelled' count on 'full' rows that use every window.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in the README table and the prose figures (55 -> 179 distance, 1.3-2.1 loss with informed prior, 12.36 vs 11.42, 0.83 vs 2.15) match results.txt; '4 tests'; runtime 'about 6 min' (5 min 07 s); the label-volume confound is disclosed (result 3). Not backed: result 1 'fails entirely with the uninformed one, where its weights end up 179 to 658 away from the oracle's and get worse with more hours' and result 2 'with the uninformed prior it is worse than the biased fit in every row ... weight distances in the thousands. The raw weights (up to 1/eps = 500) are the likely cause' (README.md:52-53) are artifacts of a non-converged solver, not properties of the estimators; 'The earlier guess confused close to the oracle on utility with unbiased' rests on those rows. Minor: 'weights within 0.3 of the oracle's' for full is 0.32 +- 0.14 at hour 20.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wants to know how much selection bias costs a self-trained always-on assistant and whether IPS helps. They would inherit a broken solver: the most striking finding (uninformed learner diverging from the oracle with more data) is not a property of the method, and the IPS-variance story is partly solver divergence. The informed-prior half survives and is a reasonable toy. Nearest prior work, none cited: Shimodaira (2000, J. Stat. Plan. Inference 90:227) on covariate shift, where a correctly specified unweighted MLE is consistent if selection depends on x only, so weighting only adds variance; here the bias arises because selection depends on the wake phrase, which is correlated with need (P(need|wake) = 0.70 by hand vs 0.03 base) and is not a feature, a mechanism the README never names. Strehl et al. 2010 (NeurIPS, learning from logged implicit exploration), Swaminathan and Joachims 2015 (CRM/POEM, and self-normalised IPS), Dudik, Langford and Li 2011 (doubly robust). The result is not new and, as reported, not sound.
evidence.domain: Against practice in off-policy learning: estimators are compared after checking the optimizer converged (gradient/objective check, or a library solver); a label-matched random-sample control isolates bias from data volume (missing, admitted); weight clipping/SNIPS are the standard baselines for IPS variance (missing, admitted); the selection mechanism is stated and the ignorability condition discussed (missing). The core departure is numerical: undamped Newton on logistic loss is known to diverge from a poor start, and its output was reported as the estimator's. The PhD bar in research/CLAUDE.md is not met.

defects.what: fit_map runs 40 undamped Newton steps with no line search and no convergence check, and diverges from the uninformed prior start and on many IPS fits: returned weights have MAP objective 450x to 360,000x the true minimum and lie 163 to 29,972 from the prior mean (any true MAP is within 33-117). The deployed learner also acts on these weights, so the logged history itself is distorted. The same solver is copied from research/ambient-ips (ips.py:46) and research/ambient-bandit (bandit.py:46).

Results 1 and 2 report optimizer artifacts as findings: the uninformed biased fit 'fails entirely' (utility 1.59/-0.15/-13.08, distance 179-658) and uninformed IPS distances in the thousands 'likely' from raw weights. With a converged solver the uninformed rows equal the informed ones (biased 10.63/10.85/11.44, IPS 9.61/11.15/12.36, distances < 3). The results table and utility.svg are not regenerated (an audit note now flags them).

Core logic untested: 4 of 5 seeded mutants survived (IPS weights prop instead of 1/prop; full fit on labelled windows only; decision rule ignoring the others cost; prior gradient centred on zero), and no test checks that fit_map's output is stationary, the check that would have caught the divergence.

No nearest prior work from off-policy learning or covariate shift (Shimodaira 2000; Strehl et al. 2010; Swaminathan and Joachims 2015; Dudik et al. 2011), and the selection mechanism is never analysed: with a correctly specified model and selection on x only, unweighted MLE is consistent; the bias here comes from always labelling wake-phrase windows (P(need|wake)=0.70), a variable not in the features. No label-matched control (admitted).

Copied engine and dead code: fit_map duplicated across three ambient projects with the same bug; run_online unused here; sigmoid clipping at +-30 removes saturated points from the Hessian; results.txt prints a 'labelled' count on 'full' rows that use all windows; 'within 0.3' for full is 0.32 at hour 20.

verdict: A tidy, reproducible toy (run.py regenerates results.txt byte for byte; the oracle weights and utility match a closed-form Bayes computation) whose central numbers are wrong. Its MAP logistic solver is undamped Newton without a line search or convergence check, and an independent line-searched solver shows it diverges: the uninformed-prior learner that 'fails entirely' and drifts 179-658 from the oracle, and the IPS fits 'thousands' away, are non-converged iterates whose objective is hundreds to hundreds of thousands of times the true minimum. With a converged solver the uninformed rows match the informed ones (biased about 10.6-11.4, IPS 9.6-12.4 utility/h, weights within 3 of the oracle). The informed-prior conclusion (bias costs 1.3-2.1 utility/h; IPS helps at eps = 0.02, is noisier at 0.002) survives. 4 of 5 seeded mutants survived the 4 tests, prior work on off-policy learning and covariate shift is not cited, and the actual bias mechanism (always labelling wake-phrase windows) is unstated. Does not meet the bar. The same solver sits in ambient-ips and ambient-bandit, which should be checked.
